title: Pushout of the etale torsor extension
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $\varphi:G\to G'$ be a morphism of abelian sheaves on $S_{\mathrm{Et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], and let $0\to G\xrightarrow{\iota}E_T\xrightarrow{\sigma}\mathbf Z_S\to0$ be the canonical extension attached to a $G$-torsor $T$ [def-sc-gm-torsor] by [lem-sc-torsor-h1]. Let $E_T\wedge^GG'=(G'\oplus E_T)/\{(\varphi(g),-\iota(g)):g\in G\}$ be its pushout along $\varphi$, with canonical maps $\iota':G'\to E_T\wedge^GG'$ and $v:E_T\to E_T\wedge^GG'$. Then there is a unique $\sigma':E_T\wedge^GG'\to\mathbf Z_S$ with $\sigma'\circ v=\sigma$ and $\sigma'\circ\iota'=0$, the sequence $0\to G'\xrightarrow{\iota'}E_T\wedge^GG'\xrightarrow{\sigma'}\mathbf Z_S\to0$ is short exact, and $(\varphi,v,\mathrm{id}_{\mathbf Z_S})$ is a morphism of short exact sequences. Its fibre over $1$ (the subsheaf of local sections mapped to $1$ by $\sigma'$, with $G'$ acting by translation through $\iota'$) is canonically the $G'$-torsor $T\wedge^GG'$, the sheafification of $(T\times G')/G$ with $g\cdot(t,g')=(g\cdot t,\varphi(g)^{-1}g')$ and $G'$ acting on the second factor. Moreover the pushout sequence is isomorphic, as an extension of $\mathbf Z_S$ by $G'$, to the canonical extension $0\to G'\to E_{T\wedge^GG'}\to\mathbf Z_S\to0$ attached to the $G'$-torsor $T\wedge^GG'$ by [lem-sc-torsor-h1].

source.place: Cohomology on Sites, Lemma 03AJ (label lemma-torsors-h1), pushout of E_T along phi is E_{T wedge G'}

proof.text: The category $\Ab(S_{\mathrm{Et}})$ of abelian sheaves on the small étale site of $S$ is an abelian category by [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. Regard $0\to G\xrightarrow{\iota}E_T\xrightarrow{\sigma}\mathbf Z_S\to0$ as a short exact sequence in it and take $u=\varphi$ in [lem-weil-pbc-pushout-short-exact-sequence]: the pushout $E_T\wedge^GG'=\operatorname{Coker}((\varphi,-\iota):G\to G'\oplus E_T)$ exists, there is a unique $\sigma'$ with $\sigma'\circ v=\sigma$ and $\sigma'\circ\iota'=0$, the sequence $0\to G'\xrightarrow{\iota'}E_T\wedge^GG'\xrightarrow{\sigma'}\mathbf Z_S\to0$ is short exact, and $(\varphi,v,\mathrm{id}_{\mathbf Z_S})$ is a morphism of short exact sequences.

source.place: Cohomology on Sites, Lemma 03AJ, pushout of E_T along phi

proof.text: Write $F'\subset E_T\wedge^GG'$ for the fibre of $\sigma'$ over $1$ and $[g',e]$ for the class of a local section $(g',e)$ of $G'\oplus E_T$. By [lem-sc-torsor-h1], $E_T$ is the quotient of $\mathbf Z[T]$ by the relations $[g\cdot t]=[t]+\iota(g)$, with $\sigma([t])=1$. Define $\alpha:T\times G'\to F'$ on local sections by $\alpha(t,g')=[g',[t]]$; it lands in $F'$ since $\sigma'[g',[t]]=\sigma([t])=1$. It is invariant under the action of $G$: $\alpha(g\cdot t,\varphi(g)^{-1}g')=[g'-\varphi(g),[t]+\iota(g)]=[g',[t]]-[\varphi(g),-\iota(g)]=[g',[t]]$, because $(\varphi(g),-\iota(g))$ lies in the image of $(\varphi,-\iota)$. It is $G'$-equivariant: $\alpha(t,g'+h)=[g',[t]]+\iota'(h)$. Hence $\alpha$ induces a $G'$-equivariant morphism of sheaves $\bar\alpha:T\wedge^GG'\to F'$ (universal property of sheafification). Now $F'$ is a $G'$-torsor: it is locally nonempty, since $T$ is locally nonempty and $\alpha(t,0)\in F'$; and if $x,y$ are local sections of $F'$, then $\sigma'(x-y)=0$, so by the exactness of Step 1 $x-y=\iota'(h)$ for a local section $h$ of $G'$, unique as $\iota'$ is injective; so $G'$ acts freely and transitively. Since $T\wedge^GG'$ is a $G'$-torsor as well, the equivariant morphism $\bar\alpha$ of $G'$-torsors is an isomorphism (locally both are $G'$ with translation, and an equivariant self-map of $G'$ is a translation). This is the canonical identification $T\wedge^GG'\cong F'$.

source.place: Cohomology on Sites, Lemma 03AJ, identification of the fibre of the pushout

proof.text: Put $T'=T\wedge^GG'\cong F'$ (Step 2). By [lem-sc-torsor-h1], $E_{T'}$ is the quotient of $\mathbf Z[T']$ by the relations $[h\cdot s]=[s]+h$ ($h$ a local section of $G'$, $s$ of $T'$), with $G'\to E_{T'}$, $h\mapsto h$, and $E_{T'}\to\mathbf Z_S$, $[s]\mapsto1$. The map $\mathbf Z[F']\to E_T\wedge^GG'$, $[s]\mapsto s$, respects these relations, since $h\cdot s=s+\iota'(h)$ in $E_T\wedge^GG'$; so it induces $\beta:E_{T'}\to E_T\wedge^GG'$ with $\beta(h)=\iota'(h)$ and $\sigma'\circ\beta=([s]\mapsto1)$. Thus $(\mathrm{id}_{G'},\beta,\mathrm{id}_{\mathbf Z_S})$ is a morphism of short exact sequences in the abelian category $\Ab(S_{\mathrm{Et}})$, and $\beta$ is an isomorphism by the five lemma. This is the isomorphism of extensions with $E_{T\wedge^GG'}$.
